Nizami Ganjavi was a 12th-century poet from Ganja, in what is now Azerbaijan, and the greatest writer of romantic epics in Persian. He lived nearly all his life in his home city, writing for princes of the states that followed the Seljuk Empire in the Caucasus and Iran.

His fame rests on the Khamsa, or "Quintet", five long poems in rhyming couplets:

  • the Treasury of Mysteries, on moral and religious themes
  • Khosrow and Shirin, the love of a Persian king and an Armenian princess
  • Layla and Majnun, the tale of a lover driven mad by love
  • the Seven Beauties, stories told to King Bahram by seven princesses
  • the Book of Alexander, on Alexander the Great as conqueror and sage

He brought a lively, realistic style to the epic form that Ferdowsi had used for the Shahnameh. Poets in Persian, Turkish and Urdu imitated the Khamsa for centuries, and its scenes were favourite subjects of Persian and Mughal painters.
